recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Only revisit if a human wants to audit or update the external Confluence resource-creation guidance mentioned in the Jira resolution; no FHIR core source follow-up is needed.
issue_request: FHIR-30696 was Published/Not Persuasive with Modification for R5. It reported that references.html#canonical appeared to have a manually maintained canonical-resource list, cited SubscriptionTopic as missing, asked for the inclusion criterion, and requested at minimum updating the table. The accepted resolution clarified that resources must inherit from CanonicalResource, not merely map to the Definition pattern, and required the references sentence to link canonical URLs to canonicalresource.html.
initial_application: The source-side application appears in git commit 3e26de4b9476e38ecc56d30600d44c52813ac066, whose subject misspelled the key as HIR-30696 but whose patch added the requested canonicalresource.html link to source/references.html. Current source retains that link and the generated [%canonical-resources%] placeholder.
additional_context: FHIR-I minutes record the issue as Not Persuasive with Modification and later include it in a TSC-delayed block vote. SubscriptionTopic is now an active resource in source/fhir.ini and its StructureDefinition inherits from CanonicalResource. A later FHIR-17537 audit preserved the same canonical-resource list as the scope anchor for canonical(Any). Targeted Zulip and Confluence searches found no conflicting community evidence; the Confluence resource-creation-page action in the Jira resolution is outside the core source checkout.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. No source edit was needed because the current source and rendered build already meet the source-side Jira resolution.

related_jiras.note: Earlier canonical(Any) guidance establishes why the references page's canonical-resource list remains the correct scope anchor; it is already represented on the combined branch.
